name: Liposuction / chin lipo

lead: Liposuction removes localized fat through a thin suction tube (cannula) inserted via small incisions. Under the chin and along the neck, the payoff people want is less submental fullness and a sharper jawline and neck angle, sometimes combined with chin surgery.

The cannula is moved through the fat layer to remove cells, often after fluid with dilute anaesthetic is injected (the tumescent technique) [11]. Removed fat cells do not regrow, though remaining fat cells can enlarge, and reference sources say overall body fat generally returns to its earlier level over months. The neck contour shows once swelling settles. A 2004 randomized study found liposuction did not alter insulin action or coronary risk factors. Evidence specific to submental liposuction comes from small registered studies and clinical practice.

paras: It is performed by a surgeon, often with local anaesthesia and sedation for small areas like the chin, and sometimes alongside a chin implant or neck lift. People wear a compression garment for a period afterward, and swelling takes weeks to settle before the final contour shows.

A 2024 meta-analysis of 39 studies and 29,368 patients found contour deformity (2.35 percent), hyperpigmentation (1.49 percent), seroma (0.65 percent) and haematoma (0.27 percent) among complications [1]. Rarer serious events include deep vein thrombosis, organ perforation and embolism, with risk rising with the volume removed [11]. It is surgery under anaesthesia and should be done by a licensed surgeon.

chain: Fat suctioned from chin and neck
angle.text: Fat is suctioned from under the chin and neck, reducing submental fullness so the jawline and neck angle look sharper. Removed fat cells do not return, and the contour shows once swelling settles.

lead: Liposuction, also called lipoplasty or suction-assisted lipectomy, is a surgical procedure in which fat is removed from beneath the skin by suction through a cannula [1]. Submental (chin) liposuction targets fat under the chin and along the neck, and in looksmaxxing communities it is discussed as a way to define the jawline and neck angle.

Wikipedia reports that the technique was developed in Rome in the mid-1970s by Arpad and Giorgio Fischer, extended to the whole body by Yves-Gérard Illouz and Fournier, and that Jeffrey Klein's tumescent method using dilute lidocaine later enabled local-anaesthesia procedures [1]. In the US it became the most commonly performed cosmetic procedure in 2015 according to the same source [1].

Reference sources say removed fat cells are permanently gone, but that overall body fat generally returns to its earlier level within months, with fat sometimes redistributing to other areas [1]. A 2004 randomized study found that removal of subcutaneous fat by liposuction did not alter insulin action or coronary heart disease risk factors [2]. The evidence base on submental liposuction specifically is limited to small registered studies and clinical practice.
infobox: Mid-1970s, Rome (Fischer); tumescent technique by Klein in the 1980s [1]
Submental and jowl fat, sometimes combined with chin surgery [7]

paras: Wikipedia describes several techniques: suction-assisted, tumescent, power-assisted, water-jet assisted, ultrasound-assisted, laser-assisted and radiofrequency-assisted liposuction [1]. A randomized study compared radiofrequency-assisted liposuction and a helium-based skin-tightening device with VASER-assisted liposuction for arm contouring [3].

According to Wikipedia, the Fischers developed a blunt cannula with suction in the mid-1970s and in 1977 reviewed 245 cases of cellulite treatment of the hip and thigh area. Illouz developed a wet technique, Fournier promoted compression after surgery, and Klein published the tumescent technique in the 1980s [1].

Liposuction is used for cosmetic body contouring and for medical indications such as lipedema, lymphedema and lipomas [1]. A systematic review of lipedema treatments found tumescent liposuction had the strongest evidence for sustained symptom improvement, though most studies were observational [4], and a randomized trial protocol compares surgery with decongestive therapy for lipedema [5]. A Danish review of gynaecomastia reports that surgical excision with liposuction can provide excellent results with a low complication rate when the glandular enlargement persists [6].

A registered study, NCT04283708, compares chin advancement genioplasty with and without submental liposuction for skeletal chin deficiency [7]. Wikipedia's article does not discuss submental liposuction specifically [1].

Wikipedia reports that evidence does not support an effect on weight beyond a couple of months, and that fat generally returns to pre-treatment levels, sometimes in other areas including visceral fat [1]. A randomized study found that liposuction did not change insulin action or risk factors for coronary heart disease [2].

A 2024 systematic review and meta-analysis of 39 studies with 29,368 patients (mean age 40.6, mean BMI 26.4) reported contour deformity at 2.35 percent, hyperpigmentation 1.49 percent, seroma 0.65 percent, haematoma 0.27 percent, superficial burn 0.25 percent and allergic reaction 0.16 percent. Wikipedia describes risk as dependent on volume, listing deep vein thrombosis, organ perforation, bleeding, infection, fat embolism, lidocaine toxicity and skin necrosis, and cites a 2011 estimate of about one death per 10,000 cases [1]. It also reports that deaths among US citizens after cosmetic surgery abroad, notably in the Dominican Republic between 2009 and 2022, were mostly attributed to embolism [1].

Studies include a 2024 meta-analysis of complications, a randomized metabolic study [2], randomized comparisons of lipedema surgery and conservative therapy [5], an arm-contouring randomized trial [3], and a registered gynaecomastia study [8]. For the face and neck, a registered study of genioplasty with and without submental liposuction is listed [7]. No published randomized trial of submental liposuction for jawline definition in young men was identified.

On looksmax.org, one poster argues that neck liposuction is a very good surgery for people who are not severely weak-jawed and says the results are permanent [9]. Other posts in the community discuss combining liposuction with genioplasty, or comparing it with fat-dissolving injections, with posters raising concerns about removing too much cheek fat.

lore.intro: Submental and neck liposuction is discussed as a durable route to a leaner lower third, with disagreement over how permanent the results are and how much fat is safe to remove [9].
